races.name: Cummersdale Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Izzari
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator on good going, trainer Jardine in fair recent form (6/30 over 14 days); 17 days since last run is fine, but stepping back from longer trips and a poor recent form string (48-00-69) makes confidence limited even if the pace collapses.
runners_data.comment: Izzari has run over today's trip and going before and, rated 73 by us against an official mark of 63, holds a clear edge on ratings; yet to win in his last six starts, he must convert that potential, though 17 days fresh he arrives in decent order.

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Excellently in-form prominent racer — two wins and nine places from 13 good-ground runs, finished second twice in her last two starts; headgear noted (hg:p), Tim Easterby yard running at 4/64 over 14 days but the individual horse's numbers are very encouraging for this shape.
runners_data.comment: Perfidia arrives on the back of back-to-back seconds two and three starts back, plus a win four starts back, showing consistent ability at this level — experience over today's trip and going adds appeal. The main risk is that seventh last time out, which must be explained away.

runners_data.name: Tees George
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with a recent second and two placed efforts from his last four, handles good ground well (10/15 sim-going hits); Adrian Nicholls yard quiet (1/7 T14) but this six-year-old travels up with the pace and Carlisle's mile suits his profile.
runners_data.comment: Tees George shaped well last time out, finishing second, and has experience of today's distance and going — his return to form makes him a genuine threat here, though he has managed just the one win in his last six outings.

runners_data.name: Hostility
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner whose style advantage is significant here — won over 8f on good, shaped well last time; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.94) notes he is arguably pushed out of his ideal front-running role by the data tag, but in practice he IS the map's pace-setter and that structural position is genuinely his to take.
runners_data.comment: Hostility warmed up for this with a win two starts back and a runner-up finish three starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the risk is that fifth last time out suggests he may need to find more on his latest evidence.

runners_data.name: Bay Dream Believer
runners_data.note: Five career wins on good ground and a natural hold-up style backed by the hg:h tag; 24 days since last run is ideal, and his two wins at 8f and 10f on good show he handles this trip — the best-credentialed closer in the field if the front end tires.
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in her last six starts, including a win last time out, Bay Dream Believer arrives on a handy 24-day break with distance and going experience in her favour; however, a rating of 64 and two mid-field finishes in between suggest she'll need to reproduce her best to figure here.

runners_data.name: Jewel Maker
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old hold-up specialist whose true racing style is deep at the rear, but with several closers competing for that ground he is likely to find himself racing wider and earlier than he would like; Tim Easterby's yard and a modest recent form string (074877) make this a tough ask at OR=55.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Jewel Maker faces an uphill task, though he has run over today's distance and going before and steps out fresh enough at 17 days between runs; carrying 132 lb from stall five, consistent improvement looks needed.

runners_data.name: Rajawail
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner in the field at OR=45, and while he is a natural hold-up type his recent form (875060) gives little reason for confidence; 56 days off the track is a significant fitness query, and racing compressed into a midfield role he would not naturally choose compounds the difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked last on our figures, Rajawail faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a 56-day break plus draw two offer minor positives, but her recent form makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Balance Of Trade
runners_data.note: A three-year-old stepping sharply down in trip from staying distances (last two runs were 16f and 17f), and though good-going experience is adequate (7/14), the combination of true hold-up style, no wins from 14 runs, and a drastic trip reduction makes this a very speculative runner in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a fifth last time out and his best recent effort a third four starts back, Balance Of Trade faces a stiff task from stall 8 carrying 118 lb — experience over today's trip and going is his main claim.

races.paceDynamic: Hostility is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press them early, Conor Whiteley should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over Carlisle's mile without being seriously challenged for the lead. Perfidia and Tees George are the most likely prominent horses to track Hostility closely, forming a small front group while the remainder of the field — Izzari, Bay Dream Believer, and the three redistributed hold-up types — settle in behind. The redistributed horses Jewel Maker, Balance Of Trade, and Rajawail are all natural hold-up operators who are mapped to midfield solely because the rear of the race is overcrowded with closers; they are unlikely to secure their preferred deep position and may find themselves racing less comfortably than their style demands. A sustainable, uncontested pace with one honest front-runner and a contested midfield favours horses that travel prominently and can sustain their effort into the home straight — the prominent profile has a clear structural edge in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hostility Dictates Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Hostility crosses cleanly and sets a measured, uncontested gallop that draws the sting from closers before the home turn.
scenarios.body: Whiteley controls tempo throughout, the pace is honest but never frantic, and Hostility's rivals who want to close are left with too little ground to make up over a mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Hit Back
scenarios.trigger: If Hostility's pace is close enough to genuine that Perfidia or Tees George can use their prominent position to wear them down in the straight.
scenarios.body: The two prominent pursuers press Hostility from the home turn, turning it into a sustained battle that rewards the best-travelled horse in the first four; Perfidia's strong recent form and good-going record make her the likeliest beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Hostility's front-running tempo is slightly too strong for the pace-setters and opens a gap for a genuinely fresh closer to finish through.
scenarios.body: Bay Dream Believer, with five wins on good ground and a proven hold-up record, is best placed among the true closers to exploit tired leaders; Izzari is the secondary threat if the pace genuinely collapses in front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded midfield causes interference or traffic problems that scramble the typical finishing order late in the race.
scenarios.body: With Balance Of Trade, Jewel Maker, and Rajawail all racing out of their natural position and likely bunched, a messy contest could shuffle the deck; any of the prominent horses avoiding trouble would gain, though the redistributed types are least likely to benefit from the confusion they may help create.

watchPoints.text: Hostility's early crossing speed will determine the entire race shape — watch whether Whiteley pushes to lead cleanly from the gate or if Perfidia and Tees George force a higher early tempo than planned.

The three redistributed hold-up horses (Jewel Maker, Balance Of Trade, Rajawail) are all likely to be racing in unfamiliar midfield territory; bunching or interference between them in the early to mid-race could compromise Bay Dream Believer and Izzari who need clear running.

Bay Dream Believer is the most powerful closer on form but needs the pace to be genuine — if Hostility idles in front and slows the middle portion of the race, the hold-up runners will have insufficient run-in to close.

Perfidia has the best recent form in the race with back-to-back placed efforts and 13 hits from 15 good-ground runs; watch how Cian Horgan (3lb claimer) positions her in the first two furlongs relative to Hostility, as a prominent sit just off the leader could prove the winning move.

Balance Of Trade dropping from marathon trips to a mile is an unusual angle worth monitoring in-running — if the horse travels with unexpected ease in the early stages it may signal the trip drop is working, though the lack of any win from 14 career starts argues against over-weighting that scenario.

races.name: National Racehorse Week 2026 EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Colin Parker Raceday 1st Nov Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Influencer Man
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose two-run form includes a 2nd over this exact 5f trip on Good — the most relevant profile in the field for this distance and going combination, and arrives fresh on 24 days' rest for Keatley whose 2/12 T14 strike-rate suggests live runners are being placed selectively.
runners_data.comment: Influencer Man shaped with plenty of promise when second last time out, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions — the main concern is that he remains winless in his last two starts.

runners_data.name: Beauty For Love
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Johnston and Orr, with Good-ground form across four runs and the highest volume of experience in this field — drops to a career-low OR of 71 but has yet to win; her chance depends entirely on whether she can control the pace rather than share it with Lauralynn.
runners_data.comment: Returned third last time out and third three starts back, but sixth two starts back highlights inconsistency; yet to win in recent starts. Has run over today's trip and returns after 25 days, though ranked fifth of seven on our ratings.

runners_data.name: Onslaught
runners_data.note: Blinkers applied and back to the 5f trip where he has twice placed on Good — Fahey yard at 3/31 T14 is ticking over and Garritty can be a patient handler; a true hold-up runner who should settle at the rear naturally, making him a legitimate finisher if the front two tire.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Onslaught has placed third in each of his last two outings but the sixth before that is a concern; ranked sixth of seven on our figures, he faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Jazz Queen
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly has the most competitive recent form in the race but is a genuine hold-up type squeezed into a midfield mapping because the field is packed with front-runners — her finishing kick is real but a 5f flat sprint on Good that is run at pace may not give her enough space to express it, and her 0/5 win record underlines the risk.
runners_data.comment: Jazz Queen has experience over today's trip and ground, shaped with promise when second four starts back, and her rating of 72 suggests she holds strong claims returning fit after 27 days; the concern is she remains winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Lauralynn
runners_data.note: Returns from 88 days off having won a 5f Tapeta race and placed twice on Good — the break is a significant unknown but Carroll's 0/6 T14 offers little confidence the yard is firing, and she must fight for the lead immediately rather than settling after a layoff.
runners_data.comment: Lauralynn was a winner two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with a rating of 74 suggesting she retains strong claims from stall 2; the main concern is that seventh last time out and 88 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Concert Pitch
runners_data.note: Versatile prominent racer with four placings from six runs at 5f, including two on Good ground — Robinson is a capable northern claimer and Ellison's 2/16 T14 represents a workmanlike level of activity; the horse's consistency makes it the most reliable profile for a contested pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Concert Pitch has been placed second in two of his last three starts and, with experience over today's trip and going, he arrives in good nick 22 days on — yet to score in recent starts, but his profile makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Excessive
runners_data.note: Three-run juvenile wearing a hood for the first time, trained by the in-form Easterby yard (4/64 T14 is high volume), and drops from 6f on a Tapeta surface back to the 5f turf trip where it was a never-nearer 4th on Soft — limited evidence but hood application and stable form are worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a ninth last time out the most damaging entry on his recent CV, Excessive is hard to fancy from seventh in our rankings; he has run over today's trip and going, which is something, but the overall profile offers little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Beauty For Love and Lauralynn are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the gates over this sharp Carlisle 5f, creating a genuinely contested early tempo rather than a solo breakaway — both have recent form that confirms they look to lead, and neither is likely to concede that role willingly. The resulting honest, pressured gallop on Good turf over a flat sprint trip will compress the field quickly and leave little room for dramatic late moves, favouring runners who can travel close to the pace without burning their own petrol. Jazz Queen is a true hold-up type who has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more prominent and rear-of-field types than the race shape can accommodate at the back — of the genuine hold-up horses, Influencer Man and Onslaught are the most likely to actually settle in the rear positions. The tactical verdict is clear: a contested lead benefits prominent-to-midfield closers who can time a run off a genuine gallop — those with the tactical versatility to sit second or third and pounce at the furlong pole are most advantaged, while deep closers face a short enough track to struggle if gaps don't open.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Beauty For Love and Lauralynn fight for the front and set an honest tempo that stretches the field early.
scenarios.body: The pressured pace drains both leaders in the final furlong, leaving a prominent-tracking horse to pick them off close home on this flat 5f track. Concert Pitch, with multiple placed efforts at 5f on Good ground and a handy draw, is ideally profiled to sit just off the heat and pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Gets Easy Toe
scenarios.trigger: If Lauralynn (88 days off, dropping back from 7f win) or Beauty For Love gains an uncontested lead and settles into an unchallenged rhythm.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner over a flat sprint on Good ground is notoriously difficult to reel in when the gallop is measured — the leader conserves enough for a strong final 100 yards. Beauty For Love's proven 5f exposure and Oisin Orr's big-field experience give her the edge if she secures a soft lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn each other out entirely and the pace collapses in the final furlong, creating a genuine vacuum.
scenarios.body: Influencer Man and Onslaught, genuinely held up off the pace, would need a strong finishing run in a compressed 5f sprint — achievable only if the tempo is truly scorching and the field fans wide. This scenario is tempered by Jazz Queen's redistribution tag, as that horse is not a true deep closer and its presence at the back is a map artefact rather than a tactical reality.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexposed Type Sprints Clear
scenarios.trigger: If a lightly-raced or returning runner — particularly Lauralynn returning from 88 days — finds an unexpected gear on fresh legs.
scenarios.body: Lauralynn won at 5f on Standard and placed on Good, and a fit-again performance after a break could see her outsprint the field if rivals are preoccupied with each other. Excessive, wearing a hood and having only three career runs with unexplored ceiling, is the other wildcard in this shape if the pace suits a late surge from mid-division.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Lauralynn and Beauty For Love genuinely fight for the front from the break — if both are ridden positively, the resulting pace war could light up the first 2f and dramatically shorten the finishing effort of all runners, making any prominent-tracking horse a significant danger.

Lauralynn returns from 88 days off and must immediately find her stride into a contested early position — if she's ring-rusty out of the gates, her tactical role evaporates and Beauty For Love may get an easier lead than the race shape implies.

Jazz Queen is mapped to midfield but is a confirmed hold-up type — watch where Hart actually positions her; if she settles deep she may not have enough 5f track left to reel in the leaders, and her STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 signals a meaningful discount to her chances in this shape.

Onslaught wears a hood (blinkers) for the first time and is back at 5f where all his placed efforts have come — headgear plus trip return is a combination worth monitoring in the pre-race market for any market support suggesting stable confidence.

Excessive's hood application on debut at this shorter trip for a high-volume yard is a low-key flag — Easterby's 4/64 T14 means plenty of runners but the deliberate headgear change on a lightly-raced juvenile on a drop to 5f turf is worth a line.

races.name: Christmas Community Raceday 13th Dec Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jenever
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by Jessica Macey, 21 days since last run, consistent recent form at 6f on Good going (11 wins or places from 15 similar-going runs) though has not won since July — likely finishes into the frame rather than threatens.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six, Jenever nonetheless brings distance and going experience, a sharp 21-day turnaround and a promising speed rating of 89 that outstrips his official mark — the third last time out the most encouraging sign; the risk is that elusive winning form.

runners_data.name: Sixtygeesbaby
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 4yo wears a tongue-tie and visor, has race fitness from 21 days ago, and has been consistent at 6f on Good but has not won this season — the sole front-runner, she controls this race from the front and her STYLE_FIT flag at 0.92 is largely irrelevant as she is simply running her natural role.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Sixtygeesbaby nevertheless catches the eye as the top-rated runner here, with his speed rating of 86 pointing to untapped potential; he has experience of today's trip and going, and 21 days between runs leaves him fresh.

runners_data.name: Stirrup Cup
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby runner returning after 55 days off, best recent form is a win on Soft and placed efforts on Good at 6f — the longer layoff is a mild concern but the course and distance profile is solid with a tongue-tie worn.|
runners_data.comment: Stirrup Cup landed a win two starts back but has since finished fifth, and 55 days off the track is a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 140 lb from stall eight.

runners_data.name: Another Investment
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's 7yo has been remarkably consistent, placing in three consecutive runs on Good at 6f, but is flagged as fading in finishes — a hold-up style animal who is fresh off a 10-day turnaround and is best suited when pace is honest enough to reel in the leaders.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent without being a winner, Another Investment has finished second in three of his last five starts and has run over today's trip and going before; winless in recent starts, he carries 139 lb from stall three, but his current form gives him every chance of finally getting his head in front.

runners_data.name: Maldevious
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's 4yo won at 6f on Good 10 days ago wearing a tongue-tie and cheekpieces, is a naturally prominent racer with strong recent form — a key player in the race shape and arguably the most dangerous challenger to Sixtygeesbaby.|
runners_data.comment: Maldevious arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her solid claims here; third three starts back adds further encouragement, though her two ninths in recent starts are the form query to overcome.

runners_data.name: Great
runners_data.note: Sam England's 4yo is a genuine hold-up horse with wins at 5f and 6f on Good (3W5P from 15 similar-going runs), but the redistribution note reflects that in a field already packed with rear-runners, it cannot secure its natural position — fresh from 6 days ago and its best form is over 5f.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten fifth and seventh in his last six starts offset the two wins in that span, and carrying 137 lb from stall nine on a mark of 65 makes this a tough ask; he has run over today's trip and going before, but ranked seventh of nine on our figures, he's hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 4yo has course form over 7f on Standard and placed efforts at that trip, but its going stats at Good (5/15 0W0P) are the weakest in the field — naturally a hold-up horse whose style is further compromised by redistribution into an unnatural midfield slot.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a pair of seconds the only bright spots amid a sequence that reads poorly, and an eighth last time out just five days ago gives little confidence she's on the upgrade; she has run over today's trip and going, but remains hard to fancy ranked last on our figures.

runners_data.name: Showtown
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 3yo carries the lowest weight at 130lbs with a hood, returning after 41 days — showed placed form at 6f on Soft but Good going stats (3/9 0W1P) are modest; a naturally prominent type who can sit close to Sixtygeesbaby and represents each-way interest if her form translates to these conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Showtown has slipped back over his last three starts — fourth and fifth before an eighth last time — and has experience of today's distance and going; carrying 130 lb from stall four, he looks a lively threat, though 41 days off and being winless in recent starts are the concerns to weigh.

runners_data.name: Valentine Catcher
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 5yo has run exclusively over 7f-8f in recent outings, dropping to 6f here is a trip question — a natural hold-up horse pushed into midfield by redistribution, with zero wins or places from 15 similar-going runs, making this a tough ask at OR 62.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a third three runs back his only recent encouragement, Valentine Catcher has since finished seventh and ninth, and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, he faces a stiff task off 129 lb from stall seven.

races.paceDynamic: Sixtygeesbaby is the lone confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 6f handicap at Carlisle on Good ground, and with no rival prepared to seriously contest the lead, she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, controlled tempo that suits her own end-to-end stamina rather than punishing anything. Maldevious and Showtown are the other prominent types who will sit close to the pace, meaning the front two or three furlong positions are essentially decided before the stalls open. This field contains more pace-hungry and hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Pickersgill, Great, and Valentine Catcher are all natural come-from-behind horses who will be shuffled forward into a midfield position they do not naturally inhabit, diluting the finishing kick they would ordinarily generate. With a single uncontested leader setting a measured tempo and the genuine hold-up horses displaced from their preferred position, this race shape most favours horses who travel prominently or in a close-up tracking role and can sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — those with the ability to sit second or third and pounce are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Sixtygeesbaby bowls along uncontested and the pace is steady enough that no closer can generate a meaningful finishing burst.
scenarios.body: Sixtygeesbaby dictates throughout on Good ground over her favoured 6f trip, and with the real hold-up horses displaced from the back, there is no late closing wave to run her down in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or tracking type sits just off Sixtygeesbaby and produces a decisive surge approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Maldevious, who won over this course and distance in Good conditions, or Showtown off the back of a quiet run are ideally positioned to strike from a close-up slot without having to make up ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses slightly in the straight, creating a gap for a horse running from further back than its natural position.
scenarios.body: Another Investment has been consistently placed in this grade on Good ground and could benefit if Sixtygeesbaby ties up late, though the redistribution of true closers into midfield means fewer horses will actually finish from off the pace than the field composition suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Crowded Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the over-populated midfield causes traffic issues and the race is run at an unusually honest pace that compresses the field.
scenarios.body: Stirrup Cup, with a recent win on soft and placed runs on Good, could emerge if pace judgement breaks down, while Great's natural hold-up style is compromised by its midfield placement making a winning run from this scenario the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Sixtygeesbaby is the sole front-runner and if she is allowed to stride clear unchallenged in the first two furlongs, the rest of the field will be chasing a ghost — watch whether Maldevious or Showtown actively try to close the gap before the turn.
Pickersgill's going stats (0W0P from 15 runs on Good) are significantly inferior to rivals — if the ground is playing truly Good, it is effectively a non-factor despite its handicap mark.
Another Investment's fading-in-finish flag is critical in a race where the pace may be genuinely steady — if Sixtygeesbaby idles in front, the closer never gets the run it needs to reel her in.

Valentine Catcher's drop from 7f-8f to 6f in recent races is a potential trip mismatch — watch in-running to see whether James Sullivan pushes to sit closer than usual or accepts a rear position that this horse cannot recover from at the shorter trip.

Great and Pickersgill are both redistributed hold-up horses whose true style cannot be expressed today — if either makes an unexpectedly forward move from the stalls, it would change the race shape significantly and may signal that jockeys have been briefed to adapt.

races.name: Ladies Night 2027 On Sale Now Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Talismans Time
runners_data.note: Active yard (T14: 7/28), 4yo who has won on Good at 13f and placed at 16f in similar conditions — a natural front-runner who will go straight to the lead and whose sim-going record of 2W3P gives genuine confidence in this ground; the contest with Savrola for the lead is the key early question.
runners_data.comment: Talismans Time landed a win in his last five starts and shaped with promise when third two runs back, and with experience over today's trip and going under his belt, he looks the one to beat here off 142 lb despite the pulled-up effort three starts back.

runners_data.name: Savrola
runners_data.note: 7yo veteran front-runner returning after 45 days off for a yard that runs its horses infrequently (T14: 0/0), which is a mild fitness query; his best form is on Soft and Standard, and his record on Good (1W2P from 9 runs) is workable but clearly weaker — he'll press for the lead but may not sustain it as effectively as on softer surfaces.
runners_data.comment: Savrola showed his best when winning and running second in recent starts, and has experience of today's trip and conditions — but his last two outings have been below par, and he'll need to bounce back sharply to justify his place as one of the chief dangers here.

runners_data.name: Shipshape
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a striking recent form string (212112), handling Good ground and distances from 12f to 16f with equal authority — Oisin Orr takes over and the horse wears headgear (p), suggesting he's held up slightly more than he'd naturally want; best positioned to exploit a contested pace from a tracking role.
runners_data.comment: Shipshape boasts a rich recent record — a winner two starts back and again three starts back, with a runner-up finish last time out underscoring his consistency — and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the 45-day absence is the one factor to weigh.

runners_data.name: Dance Time
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Loughnane who has shown only one placed effort in 15 sim-going starts and whose recent form includes a void run (V) and a string of mid-pack finishes at this trip — the pace profile suits the style but the form makes it hard to elevate above the likelier prominent types.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Dance Time heads here ranked seventh of eight on our figures, with her recent form including a void run and finishes as low as ninth — the third two runs back offers faint encouragement, but 133 lb makes life harder still.

runners_data.name: Ludo's Landing
runners_data.note: Hold-up 6yo in cheekpieces (b) who has been placed on Good ground and ran just 10 days ago — Johnston's yard is in exceptional form (T14: 6/46) and Jason Hart rides, giving trainer/jockey confidence; this horse needs the pace to collapse and currently sits closer to midfield in the map than natural, but the yard angle is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Ludo's Landing arrives in good order on just 10 days' rest and has run over today's distance and going before, but he's winless in his last six starts — a third coming four starts back is the lone bright spot in a sequence of mid-pack efforts, and carrying 132 lb won't help.

runners_data.name: Gibside
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent 7yo has genuine Good-ground form (3/14f/GOO, 3/14f/SOF) and Fentiman stays on; his natural style is hold-up and this race shape does not serve that well — the contested pace by two confirmed front-runners means he is likely to arrive late into a race already decided, and the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.92 is warranted.
runners_data.comment: Gibside shaped with real promise when third last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, with our rating of 79 suggesting he holds more in hand than his official mark of 70 implies; the concern is he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Asia Force
runners_data.note: 3yo Burke runner who has placed in every career start (22234) and steps up significantly in trip to 1m6f — her form has all been at 10-12f and the distance is an unknown, but if she stays the extra ground her consistency gives her a live chance in a late-run scenario; 41 days off and a light weight (128lbs) make the fitness question manageable.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without converting, Asia Force has finished second three times in his last five starts but remains yet to win, and 41 days off the track is a minor query; he has run over today's going before and his speed figure of 83 offers some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Ouro Preto
runners_data.note: Jardine runner who has failed to place in any of his last five starts across Good and Standard surfaces, with recent efforts reading 9th, 11th, 9th, 7th, 9th — a genuine hold-up type placed in midfield in this map because the race has more closers than positions, and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 honestly reflects that even a pace collapse may not bring him into contention given his form trajectory.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with finishes including two ninths and two sevenths, Ouro Preto is hard to fancy ranked last on our figures here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and is at least fit, reappearing just 10 days after his latest effort.

races.paceDynamic: Talismans Time and Savrola are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the jump over this 1m6f trip at Carlisle, creating a genuinely competitive early gallop rather than a dawdle — on Good ground over this distance, that honest pace will be sustained and will test resolution in the closing stages. Shipshape and Dance Time press from the prominent position, meaning the first four slots in the running order are effectively claimed, which compresses the mid-to-rear section of the field. The race shape overwhelmingly favours a strong-travelling prominent racer who can sit just off the contested lead, conserve energy through the middle mile, and produce a sustained gallop home rather than a sprint — pure hold-up horses arriving late will need the pace to collapse, which two genuine front-runners makes unlikely. Gibside and Ouro Preto are true hold-up horses whose natural position at the rear cannot be accommodated in this race shape; the contested lead means they are unlikely to arrive in time, and Shipshape or Dance Time are the likeliest beneficiaries of tracking a genuine pace from a covered position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Talismans Time and Savrola fight it out up front and a prominent tracker sustains a gallop through the dip to the line.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other up over the final mile, leaving the race to a horse travelling smoothly just behind who avoids the firefight and strikes entering the straight; Shipshape's consistent form figures across similar Good-ground distances make this profile the natural landing spot.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Talismans Time breaks cleanly and asserts early enough to dictate solo, forcing Savrola to settle for second.
scenarios.body: A lead horse who controls tempo can dictate the fractions over 1m6f and hold on when rivals cannot accelerate past; Talismans Time's two wins and three placed runs in sim-going conditions and an in-form Bethell yard back this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Talismans Time and Savrola go too hard and blow up inside the final two furlongs, opening the door for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: A genuine collapse of the front two is required here, which is possible but not the likeliest read on Good ground at a track that tends to reward gallopers; Asia Force, stepping up in trip with a string of placed efforts, is the most credible beneficiary with Ludo's Landing also in the frame.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Modest Gallop, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner is sufficiently committed early and the field bunches into a slow-run mile-and-three-quarter affair that becomes a dash.
scenarios.body: A slow pace over 1m6f is genuinely unlikely with two habitual front-runners entered, but if it materialises the race opens up for those with finishing speed; Gibside and Ouro Preto, though redistributed from their natural position, would at least face a fairer test of pace in this shape, though their STYLE_FIT discount limits confidence.

watchPoints.text: Watch the early exchanges between Talismans Time and Savrola — if they lock horns aggressively for the lead in the first half-mile over 1m6f on Good ground, both are at risk of blowing up, which would dramatically open the race for Shipshape tracking just behind.

Asia Force's stamina for 1m6f is completely unproven having never raced beyond 12f — if she weakens in the final two furlongs after travelling smoothly, it will be a trip question rather than a class or going concern.

Savrola's 45-day absence for a handler with zero runners in the past 14 days (T14: 0/0) is a legitimate fitness flag — he may be sharp enough to compete early but could stop quickly if short of peak fitness over this stamina-testing trip.

Ludo's Landing ran just 10 days ago and Charlie Johnston's yard is firing at 13% over 14 days (6/46) — if Jason Hart is riding to instructions and settles this horse closer than usual, the yard's current form deserves respect even if the race shape is not ideally set up for a hold-up type.

Shipshape's headgear (p — presumably a hood or visor) is worth monitoring in the paddock; if it settles him into a prominent but relaxed early position, his consistent 1W3P sim-going record and recent 1-2-1-2 form string make him the horse whose trajectory through the race is worth tracking throughout.

races.name: Racing Again Wednesday 19th August Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Viviana
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Charlie Johnston in fair form (three places from five recent starts); Oisin Orr's booking adds quality, and four of her five recent runs have come on Good ground with a place finish at this course and distance trip; no style concerns here.
runners_data.comment: Viviana has been placed in two of her last five starts and returns after 28 days off with experience of today's distance and going in her favour; the risk is that she's winless in recent starts and must convert consistency into a decisive finish from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Douwantitrightnow
runners_data.note: 57 days off the track is the main flag for Kevin Ryan's hold-up type; has placed in none of six recent runs and was ten lengths adrift on his last Good-ground start, though this is a rare occasion where the redistribution into midfield may naturally suit if the pace is strong enough.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and beaten last time out, Douwantitrightnow does at least have experience of today's trip and going, and her rating of 64 offers a sliver of hope from stall seven — though 57 days off the track is a query she needs to answer.

runners_data.name: Sparkling Pink
runners_data.note: Adriam Nicholls's filly is a genuine rear-of-field operator whose natural closing style is squeezed by the volume of hold-up horses in this race; her style_fit tag (0.92) signals she is unlikely to secure her ideal position, though she does have a win and four places from thirteen Good-ground efforts to her name.
runners_data.comment: Sparkling Pink showed up well to finish third two starts back and fourth three starts back, and her experience over today's trip and conditions makes her a genuine threat at 130 lb from stall 8 — though a seventh last time out raises a question about consistency.

runners_data.name: Storm Esme
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front runner for Tim Easterby — she will lead throughout and control the tempo, though her form string of -70858 over her last five is sobering and the style_fit tag (0.94) means her prominent role here is natural but her ability to sustain it under pressure is open to question.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Storm Esme at least has experience of today's distance and going, and 40 days off could see her come on; drawn nine carrying 135 lb, she appeals on profile despite the modest recent figures.

runners_data.name: Leelawadee
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's hold-up type showed real promise when second over 8f on Good going 26 days ago; stepping back to 7f may sharpen her finishing effort, and Mark Winn rides competently; she is one of the better-credentialled closers and most likely to get a clean passage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Leelawadee does at least bring experience of today's distance and going, and that second last time out suggests she retains ability — but the 135 lb burden may test her resolve in this company.

runners_data.name: Only Dream Big
runners_data.note: Two wins from twelve Good-ground starts including back-to-back victories, the blinkers (hg:b) are retained, and Tim Easterby's yard is 4/64 over 14 days — Ben Robinson takes the ride on a horse whose consistent finishing effort over 7-8f on Good ground makes him a credible threat if the pace is honest.
runners_data.comment: Only Dream Big won twice in her last six starts and returns quickly on 13 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going working in her favour from stall 1; the risk is that her three most recent runs have yielded three finishes outside the placings.

runners_data.name: Oasis Cover
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's horse is a genuine hold-up runner whose true rear style is mapped to midfield here due to field congestion; has two places from eight Good-ground starts, but a 0/5 trainer strike rate over 14 days tempers enthusiasm and the structural crowding of closers works against him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a seventh last time out and eighth two starts back making her hard to fancy, though she has distance and going experience and a second three starts back offers a crumb of form; drawn two carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Yoko
runners_data.note: David Loughnane's filly holds a headgear flag (hh) and is another true hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map; Clifford Lee rides, and while she has a place from six Good-ground runs, her last two starts show a drop in form and securing her natural position in a field full of closers is a real problem.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with only a second three runs back to show for it, Yoko has been largely disappointing in recent outings — a ninth last time out does her no favours here — though she has run over today's trip and going before, and returns on a quick turnaround in reasonable trim.

runners_data.name: Truly Special
runners_data.note: 64 days off the track is a significant fitness concern for John Wainwright's hold-up type; her last win was on Soft ground and she has placed just once from nine Good-ground starts, while being remapped from the rear makes her tactical situation harder still — the layoff and ground switch compound the risk.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and rated just 53 officially, Truly Special has been beaten well in her last three starts before a recent win, and 64 days off the track adds a fitness query — experience over today's trip and going is the one crumb of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Storm Esme is the lone confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will stride into a comfortable, uncontested position from the outset and control tempo on her own terms at Carlisle's 7f. The field is unusually loaded with hold-up horses — Yoko, Sparkling Pink, Oasis Cover and Truly Special are all true rear-of-field types redistributed into the midfield on the map simply because the race cannot accommodate that many closers at the back; in reality they will be competing for the same ground behind the pace. With a single pace-setter dictating a sustainable gallop over Good ground, the rail and the contour of Carlisle's straight will reward horses who travel prominently or can make smooth headway from mid-division, rather than those forced wide and late from genuine hold-up positions. This race shape decisively favours prominent racers and efficient mid-division movers who can sit just off a lone leader and pounce inside the final two furlongs; true closers are structurally disadvantaged because there are too many of them chasing the same limited finishing lane.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Esme bowls along uncontested and the midfield pack fails to coordinate a sustained challenge.
scenarios.body: Storm Esme dictates from flag to finish at a comfortable clip, never having to exert herself to hold off rivals who are either out of position or too far back to reel her in; the prominent types closest to her will be best placed to benefit if she fades.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Land The Spoils
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Esme's pace is sustainable enough to string out the field but Viviana or Leelawadee travel fluidly just behind and overhaul her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The pace suits a horse sitting a length or two off the leader travelling kindly; Viviana's prominent style and Leelawadee's recent second over 8f suggest both have the stamina and position to pounce when the front runner ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Esme sets a stronger gallop than expected and the race truly unfolds for a well-timed late run from a horse in mid-division.
scenarios.body: Only Dream Big, who has won twice over this trip on Good ground and carries the headgear flag, is ideally profiled for this shape; Douwantitrightnow could also be delivered with a well-timed run from further back if the pace genuinely sets things up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected injection of pace scrambles the race order and the true hold-up horses — Sparkling Pink, Yoko, Oasis Cover — manage to secure their natural rear position and find a clear run.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape because there are simply too many genuine closers fighting for the same small patch of late ground; the redistributed horses are structurally unlikely to all get clear runs, and the sustainable pace Storm Esme will set does not naturally set things up for deep finishers.

watchPoints.text: Storm Esme leads unopposed and could prove very hard to peg back if she dictates at a gentle enough clip — watch whether she is allowed to coast or is pushed into a stronger tempo early.

Viviana and Leelawadee are the most naturally positioned horses to capitalise if Storm Esme fades; watch their positions tracking into the straight — if either is within two lengths turning in, they are dangerous.

Only Dream Big carries blinkers and has won twice on this surface and trip; Ben Robinson will be looking to sit mid-division and deliver a clean run — watch for her making headway smoothly two furlongs out rather than being shuffled back.

Sparkling Pink, Yoko, Oasis Cover and Truly Special are all genuine hold-up types competing for the same late-race ground; if any one of them gets a clear passage on the inside, they could be deceptively dangerous at a price, but congestion makes this scenario fragile.

Douwantitrightnow returns after 57 days off for Kevin Ryan — watch whether Tom Eaves drops in quietly or is outpaced early, as his finishing form on Good ground over 7f has been modest and the layoff adds uncertainty.
